prompts.text: Take a look at this transaction export and tell me what my behavior actually looks like across the trades, not just the P&L.
prompts.note: Behavior-over-P&L review request, different phrasing from calibration set.

prompts.text: I want a quarterly review of my account. Here's the CSV covering January through March.
prompts.note: Quarterly cadence review.

prompts.text: Two weeks ago I sold half my position in a stock that had run up fast. I want to go back and check if that exit made sense given how I got in.
prompts.note: Specific partial-exit postmortem.

prompts.text: My trading journal says I 'stuck to the plan' on every trade this year, but I don't trust myself. Can you check the actual CSV against that?
prompts.note: Self-report vs. record cross-check.

prompts.text: This is week four of my review — same account as before. I have five new closed trades since the last session.
prompts.note: Returning-user weekly cadence, explicit trade count.

prompts.text: I noticed I keep buying more of a stock every time it dips another 10%. Can you pull that pattern out of my trade history and tell me if it's disciplined or just hope?
prompts.note: Self-noticed pattern, asking for record-based verdict.

prompts.text: Here's my full options and stock activity for the account. I want to know what my actual exit discipline looks like, not what I think it looks like.
prompts.note: Mixed options+equity account review.

prompts.text: I sold a position for a small gain last week and I already regret it — it kept running afterward. Was that a legitimate rule-based exit or did I just get scared?
prompts.note: Recent exit second-guessing.

prompts.text: Can you review my broker statement and flag every trade where I seem to have added risk right after a loss, like I was trying to win it back?
prompts.note: Revenge-trading pattern check.

prompts.text: I have a full year of trades from this account and I've never actually looked at them as a whole. Start from scratch and tell me what you see.
prompts.note: First-time full-year review.

prompts.text: This CSV only has BUY and SELL rows with dates and prices — no notes on why I made each trade. Can you still build a behavior review from it?
prompts.note: Bare transaction log, review still requested.

prompts.text: Last review we agreed I'd cap any single position at 15% of the account. I want to check the trades since then and see if I actually held to that.
prompts.note: Prior-commitment reconciliation, different cap value from calibration.

prompts.text: I closed three losing trades this month and I keep telling myself the market was just unusually bad. Go through the CSV and tell me if that holds up.
prompts.note: Self-excuse vs. record check.

prompts.text: Here's the statement from my new brokerage — I moved accounts mid-year, so I want the review to cover the whole picture across both exports.
prompts.note: Account-migration combined review.

prompts.text: I want to understand my own pattern around earnings season specifically — do I tend to sell right before earnings out of nerves? Here's the trade history.
prompts.note: Earnings-season-specific behavioral question.

prompts.text: Reviewing my account after a rough stretch: three trades closed at a loss in a row. I want an honest read on whether that's variance or a real behavioral issue.
prompts.note: Losing-streak review.

prompts.text: My account statement shows I doubled down on a losing position twice before finally cutting it. Walk me through whether the second add had any new justification.
prompts.note: Specific double-down sequence, retrospective.

prompts.text: It's been a month since our last session — picking the review back up with whatever's new in the account.
prompts.note: Returning-user, vaguer cadence than the calibration equivalent.

prompts.text: I want to check something specific: across my closed trades, did I actually sell winners and losers at similar speed, or do I let losers drag on?
prompts.note: Symmetry-of-exit-speed question over real closed trades.

prompts.text: Here's my brokerage CSV. Before I decide anything about next quarter, I want to understand what actually happened in the trades I already made.
prompts.note: Forward-decision gated on a prior review of completed trades.

prompts.text: I hold a starter position and I'm deciding whether now is the right time to size up to a full position. What would that do to my account?
prompts.note: Starter-to-full sizing decision.

prompts.text: This stock just dropped after a guidance cut, and I'm considering buying more because I think the market overreacted. What would that trade do to my existing exposure?
prompts.note: Guidance-cut add decision, overreaction framing.

prompts.text: I'm weighing whether to add to my position or just hold what I have — the price hasn't moved much, but I have new cash to deploy. Can you help me think through it against my current book?
prompts.note: Flat-price add-vs-hold decision with new cash.

prompts.text: My rule is I only add on a pullback of 10% or more from my last entry. It just hit exactly that. Should I actually place the order?
prompts.note: Rule-triggered add, asking whether to actually execute.

prompts.text: I'm thinking about buying into a company I've been researching for months, but I already hold a competitor. Would that be doubling down on the same bet?
prompts.note: Competitor-overlap decision before a new buy.

prompts.text: Before I add more to this losing position, I want to know honestly whether I have new evidence or I'm just trying to lower my average cost.
prompts.note: Evidence-vs-cost-basis self-check before an add.

prompts.text: I'm considering trimming a position that's now my largest holding after a big run-up. What would trimming it down to my target weight actually look like?
prompts.note: Trim decision to reach a target weight.

prompts.text: I want to put my next paycheck's savings into an existing position instead of starting something new. Walk me through what that does to my concentration.
prompts.note: Future-cash-flow allocation decision.

prompts.text: Is this the moment to cut my losses on this position, or does my own rule say I should give it more room first?
prompts.note: Stop-loss timing decision, rule-referencing.

prompts.text: I already have a large ETF position and I'm considering also buying the sector's top individual stock directly. Would that be redundant exposure?
prompts.note: ETF-plus-single-name overlap decision.

prompts.text: I'm thinking about adding to this position after two quarters of it going nowhere. What does my history with this exact stock say about doing that again?
prompts.note: Stagnant-position add decision, history-aware.

prompts.text: Before I buy more, I want to check: would this trade push any single sector past what I'd consider safe for my account?
prompts.note: Sector-concentration check before a buy.

prompts.text: I've got a big cash balance from a bonus and I'm deciding between adding to my highest-conviction position or diversifying into something new. What does each path do to my risk?
prompts.note: Windfall-cash decision between two contemplated trades.

prompts.text: This would break my rule about not adding within a week of an earnings report. I'm tempted anyway — what's actually at stake if I do it?
prompts.note: Rule-breaking temptation before an add, asking for the consequence.

prompts.text: I'm considering selling half of a long-held winner to reduce concentration, but I'm not sure if it still counts as 'letting a winner run' if I trim it. What would half a trim change?
prompts.note: Partial-trim decision on a long-held winner.

prompts.text: My thesis when I bought was a specific product launch. That launch just got delayed. Should I still add here, or does that change the calculus?
prompts.note: Thesis-invalidation check before an add.

prompts.text: I want to know before I click buy: does this order make my portfolio's cash cushion too thin given my other rules?
prompts.note: Pre-order cash-buffer check.

prompts.text: I'm thinking about re-entering a position I exited a few months ago at a loss. Would going back in now conflict with why I sold in the first place?
prompts.note: Re-entry decision, consistency-with-prior-exit check.

prompts.text: I have two ways to deploy new cash — top up an existing position or open a small starter position in something new. Which one keeps me inside my own risk limits?
prompts.note: Two-option cash-deployment decision, rule-bounded.

prompts.text: Before I average down again, I want an honest check: has anything actually changed since my last add, or would this just be a fourth attempt at the same bet?
prompts.note: Repeated averaging-down self-check before a fourth add.

prompts.text: What are the best AI stocks to buy this year?
prompts.note: Asks for a general 'best of' ranking, not a decision about a specific contemplated trade against the user's own holdings.

prompts.text: Should I put my money into stocks or bonds at my age?
prompts.note: Generic asset-allocation advice tied to demographics, not a specific security or an actual position being weighed.

prompts.text: What's a reasonable position size for a single stock, as a rule of thumb?
prompts.note: Asks for a generic sizing heuristic, not evaluation of an actual contemplated trade against the user's real book.

prompts.text: What do you think of Tesla's current valuation?
prompts.note: Valuation opinion question with no purchase intent or book reference — equity research, not a pre-trade evaluation.

prompts.text: What's historically been a good entry point for buying gold?
prompts.note: Generic historical pattern question about an asset class, not the user's own contemplated trade.

prompts.text: What's the difference between panic selling and disciplined stop-loss selling?
prompts.note: Definitional distinction using review-adjacent vocabulary, no reference to the user's own trade history.

prompts.text: I've had a rough month watching my portfolio value swing around.
prompts.note: Emotional market commentary with no explicit ask to review specific trades — a lead-in, not a review request.

prompts.text: How should I structure a trading journal so I actually stick with it?
prompts.note: Process/tooling question about journaling, not a request to review trades that already happened.

prompts.text: What does a good trade postmortem usually cover?
prompts.note: Meta question about the format of a postmortem in general, not a request for one on the user's own trades.

prompts.text: What's a typical drawdown before retail investors start panic selling?
prompts.note: Generic statistics-of-investor-behavior question, not a review of the user's own account.

prompts.text: What's the Fed expected to do with interest rates at the next meeting?
prompts.note: Macro/rate-forecast question with no trade or portfolio framing.

prompts.text: Explain covered calls to me.
prompts.note: Options-strategy education request; the issue's own canonical example.

prompts.text: Why did the market drop today?
prompts.note: Market-event explanation request, no personal position.

prompts.text: What's the outlook for semiconductor stocks this year?
prompts.note: Sector-outlook research question, no purchase or review framing.

prompts.text: What's the difference between a Roth IRA and a traditional IRA?
prompts.note: Account-type/tax education question, unrelated to a specific trade or review.

prompts.text: What does a P/E ratio actually tell you about a stock?
prompts.note: Valuation-metric glossary question.

prompts.text: Which sectors are outperforming the market this quarter?
prompts.note: Market-breadth research question, no personal position.

prompts.text: What is dollar-cost averaging?
prompts.note: Investing-strategy definitional question.

prompts.text: How do I read a candlestick chart?
prompts.note: Charting-education question, no trade or review context.

prompts.text: What's the historical average annual return of the US stock market?
prompts.note: General market-statistics question.
